name: durnel
author: transport-maps-journeys
description:
durnel v1 (direction: transport, maps and journeys) - A ROAD WITH LOW BRIDGES, AND THE LORRIES THAT TURN ROUND. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = THE ROAD DRAWN FROM THE SIDE, plus one caption line "<n> turn".
  M picture rows (3-6 after blank rows above the tallest thing are trimmed), then a line of "=" as
  wide as the picture (the tarmac), then the caption "<n> turn".
  bottom picture row = the ground: "." is open road, a lorry occupies exactly three columns.
  A LORRY of height h is a solid block of its own capital letter, three columns wide and h rows tall,
  standing on the ground row; its NOSE replaces one end of its bottom row: "TT>" faces right,
  "<TT" faces left. Heights 1..M-1 are uniform-random and GIVEN by the drawing - there is no height
  formula to hunt (that red herring ate fennick v2's losing player's whole game).
  A BRIDGE is a beam of 3-4 "#" at one row; the number of free rows between the beam and the ground
  row is its CLEARANCE k (2..M-2). 6-7 lorries, 3-4 beams, width 33-52 columns, clue 167-414 chars.
  Beams and lorries NEVER share a column (every drawn item is separated by >=1 blank column) and both
  ends of the road are open tarmac. Load-bearing: it makes a lorry's height simply "the non-blank cells
  in its middle column", keeps the scorer at 497 chars, and lets it index two columns either side of a
  lorry without a bounds test. Do not relax it.

ANSWER = THE CLUE'S PICTURE WITH THE TURNING LORRIES' NOSES SWAPPED END FOR END ("TT>" <-> "<TT").
Nothing else changes: same rows, same beams, same tarmac, same letters, same columns. Two characters
move per turning lorry, so the answer is UNIQUE per clue. The trailing "<n> turn" line may be kept or
dropped; both score 1 (house rule 2026-09-05).

RULE (one clause): A LORRY TURNS ROUND IFF THERE IS A BRIDGE IT CANNOT FIT UNDER SOMEWHERE AHEAD OF
IT, IN THE DIRECTION ITS NOSE POINTS. "Cannot fit" is strict: clearance < height, so a lorry exactly
as tall as the clearance drives through. Said in one breath: "it turns back if there's a bridge that
way it can't get under." It is a JOURNEY rule, not a neighbour rule - the question is whether the
lorry can reach the end of the road on the side it is facing, so the whole road ahead counts and the
road behind counts for nothing. That is the structural difference from fennick (local, two slots
either side) and from virel (a pairing between two rows).

EVERY DEMO TEACHES THE WHOLE RULE. generate() plants, in every instance (audited over 4000 clues,
100 % of the n>0 clues carry all five; the n=0 clues carry P2/P3/P4):
  P1  a lorry that turns because of a LATER beam - it clears the first bridge ahead of it and is
      stopped by one further down the road      -> kills "it only looks at the next bridge"  (100 %)
  P2  a lorry standing with a too-low beam BEHIND it                                          (100 %)
      -> kills "any low bridge in the picture" and kills the mirrored rule
  P3  a lorry standing under a beam of EXACTLY its own height -> kills "<=" instead of "<"    (100 %)
  P4  a lorry standing with a beam ahead and room to spare -> kills "a bridge ahead is enough"(100 %)
  P5  a STANDING lorry taller than a TURNING one -> kills "the N tallest turn"                (100 %)
  and, when n>=2, turners facing both ways and standers facing both ways (100 %), so "all the
  left-facing ones" is visibly wrong. The demo is a picture pair differing only in n noses.

THE FOOTHOLD (lever 7). 11.7 % of clues (measured over 4000 seeds) say "0 turn": nothing turns and the
correct answer IS the clue returned unchanged, with the caption kept or dropped. A demo-less player who
reads "a road, some lorries, some bridges, 3 turn" off the clue and echoes the picture therefore scores
~12 %, and so does every count-based guess ("the 3 tallest", "the 3 nearest a bridge") - they all agree
with the rule exactly on the zero clues. The cost is that ~13 % of demo requests land on a road where
nothing turns; that demo still teaches the drawing convention and the copy-the-caption rule.

WITNESS TABLE (2000 fresh clues, shipped scorer. Templates render with the TRUE drawing convention,
i.e. they model a player who has seen a demo and holds the wrong rule):
  clue returned unchanged                                  11.9 %   <- the foothold
  clue unchanged, caption dropped                          11.9 %   <- same thing, lenient form
  flip the N tallest lorries                               11.9 %
  flip the N shortest lorries                              11.9 %
  flip the first N lorries, left to right                  15.6 %
  N random lorries                                         16.7 %
  each lorry flipped with probability 1/2                   0.9 %
  flip every lorry                                          0.0 %
  taller than the lowest beam anywhere (direction ignored)   0.0 %
  blocked ahead OR behind (direction ignored)               0.0 %
  mirrored rule: a too-low beam BEHIND it                    0.0 %
  blocked by the NEXT beam ahead only                      11.9 %
  a beam of equal height also blocks (<= instead of <)       0.0 %
  any beam at all ahead of it                                0.0 %
  all the left-facing lorries                                0.0 %
  taller than the average clearance                          1.2 %
  taller than the median lorry height                        0.2 %
  taller than the nearest beam on either side                2.2 %
  off-by-one: h > clearance+1 blocks                        18.4 %
  off-by-one: h+1 > clearance blocks                         0.0 %
  blocked by a beam ahead WITHIN 12 COLUMNS                 30.7 %   <- the top rival
  copy the demo's flip pattern by ordinal position           3.5 %
  demo replay (another clue's answer)                        0.0 %
  one fixed real answer for every clue                       0.0 %
  junk / empty / "1"*100 / half the picture / the caption     0.0 %
  TRUE RULE (solve)                                        100.0 %
No template exceeds ~31 %. The two that pay - "only beams within a dozen columns count" (31 %) and the
clearance off-by-one (18 %) - are the intended gradient: a wrong-but-close rule scores like a good
foothold, the exact rule scores 100 %, and both are contradicted by the P1 plant in any demo whose
blocking beam happens to be far away. Everything that ignores the NOSE is at 0 %.

WELL-FORMEDNESS (18 hand-built attacks, 300 clues each, all 0 unless noted): no tarmac row, two tarmac
rows, tarmac of dashes, tarmac one column short, a blank row added on top, picture rows reversed, the
picture mirrored left-right, every nose flipped on top of the answer, dots replaced by spaces in the
ground row, letters lowercased, beams erased, the caption's count changed, the answer plus a junk line,
4000 chars of junk, noses replaced by "v", the empty string. "Caption forced to 0 turn" scores on 12 %
of clues because on those clues it IS the caption. Declared leniencies: trailing newlines and trailing
whitespace on any row, and the caption line present or absent. Nothing about the rule can be smuggled
through them: the scorer rebuilds the whole expected picture from the clue and compares row by row.

ENGINEERING (4000 fresh seeds). generate mean 0.20 ms, p99 0.74 ms, max 1.38 ms, 0 fallback uses,
3000/3000 clues distinct and deterministic; solve mean 0.026 ms; score mean 0.051 ms on real answers
and 0.025 ms on junk (including 4000-char junk and a 40x60 block of "#"); scorer 497/512 chars, solve
1336, clue 167-414 chars, solution 167-414 chars. solve() output is forced (the answer is unique), but
it varies across clues in every way that matters: 3000/3000 distinct, n in {0,2,3,4}, both nose
directions among the flips, and the flipped set is never the tallest/shortest/first-N lorries.

INTENDED SPLIT. With a demo: the diff between the two pictures is the whole rule, and a player who
reads it as a picture ("that one turned round - oh, there's a bridge that way it can't get under")
has it inside two rounds; a player who reads it as bookkeeping lands on "the N tallest" or "the N
nearest a bridge", which score exactly the foothold, or on the distance-window rule at 31 %.
Without a demo: the clue is already a drawn road with a verb and a count, so a well-formed attempt is
obvious (send the picture back with some noses swapped) and the "0 turn" instances pay ~12 %.

LEVERS. Too easy: (a) require the caption dropped, which removes the identity foothold and the offline
checksum; (b) let a beam sit directly over a lorry, so the height read costs a probe and the "no shared
columns" regularity goes; (c) also stop a lorry that would have to reverse past another lorry. Too hard:
draw one already-turned lorry into the clue as a worked instance, or drop to two beams.
generate:
# A ROAD WITH LOW BRIDGES. Lorries (3 columns wide, h rows tall, nose ">" or "<" on the
# bottom row) stand on the road; "#" beams span it overhead with a clearance of k free
# rows. Beams and lorries never share a column, and both ends of the road are clear.
# Every clue plants the four near-misses (see description): P1 a turner blocked by a
# LATER beam, P2 a stander with a too-low beam BEHIND it, P3 a stander that exactly
# fits, P4 a stander with room to spare. ~12 % of clues say "0 turn".
FB = '  BBB      ###                  TTT\n  BBB ####     SSS     HHH      TTT  ####\n  BBB          SSS WWW HHH      TTT\n..<BB..........<SS.WW>.HH>.LL>..TT>........\n===========================================\n3 turn'


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    AL = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRSTUVW"
    zero = r.random() < 0.12                      # decided once, before any retry
    for _ in range(400):
        M = r.randint(6, 7)                       # picture rows; max lorry height M-1
        hm = M - 1
        nL = r.randint(6, 7)
        nB = r.randint(3, 4)
        seq = ["L"] * nL + ["B"] * nB
        r.shuffle(seq)
        wid = [3 if t == "L" else r.choice((3, 4)) for t in seq]
        k = len(seq)
        gaps = [1] * (k + 1)                      # >=1 blank column between every drawn item
        for _ in range(r.randint(4, 10)):
            gaps[r.randrange(k + 1)] += 1
        W = sum(wid) + sum(gaps)
        pos = []
        x = gaps[0]
        for i, (t, w) in enumerate(zip(seq, wid)):
            pos.append((t, x, w))
            x += w + gaps[i + 1]
        cl = [r.randint(2, M - 2) if t == "B" else 0 for t, _, _ in pos]
        Bs = [i for i, p in enumerate(pos) if p[0] == "B"]
        Ls = [i for i, p in enumerate(pos) if p[0] == "L"]

        def info(i, d):
            ah = [cl[b] for b in Bs if (b > i if d > 0 else b < i)]
            if d < 0:
                ah = ah[::-1]                     # nearest first
            bh = [cl[b] for b in Bs if (b < i if d > 0 else b > i)]
            return (min(ah) if ah else 9, ah[0] if ah else 9, min(bh) if bh else 9)

        IN = {(i, d): info(i, d) for i in Ls for d in (1, -1)}

        H, D = {}, {}
        order = Ls[:]
        r.shuffle(order)
        need = ["P3", "P2", "P4"] if zero else ["P1", "P3", "P2", "P4"]
        ok = True
        for role in need:
            done = False
            for i in order:
                if i in H:
                    continue
                for d in r.sample((1, -1), 2):
                    mnA, fa, mnB = IN[i, d]
                    hi = min(mnA, hm)
                    if role == "P1":              # turns because of a LATER beam
                        if mnA < fa and mnA + 1 <= min(fa, hm):
                            H[i] = r.randint(mnA + 1, min(fa, hm)); done = True
                    elif role == "P3":            # stands under a beam of exactly its height
                        if mnA <= hm:
                            H[i] = mnA; done = True
                    elif role == "P2":            # stands, but a too-low beam is BEHIND it
                        if mnB + 1 <= hi:
                            H[i] = r.randint(mnB + 1, hi); done = True
                    else:                         # P4: stands with room to spare ahead
                        if mnA < 9 and min(mnA - 1, hm) >= 1:
                            H[i] = r.randint(1, min(mnA - 1, hm)); done = True
                    if done:
                        D[i] = d
                        break
                if done:
                    break
            if not done:
                ok = False
                break
        if not ok:
            continue
        H0 = dict(H); D0 = dict(D)
        good = False
        for _ in range(15):                       # re-roll the free lorries, keep the layout
            H = dict(H0); D = dict(D0)
            for i in Ls:
                if i in H:
                    continue
                d = r.choice((1, -1))
                mnA = IN[i, d][0]
                if not zero and mnA < hm and r.random() < 0.5:
                    H[i] = r.randint(mnA + 1, hm)
                else:
                    H[i] = r.randint(1, min(mnA, hm))
                D[i] = d
            T = [i for i in Ls if H[i] > IN[i, D[i]][0]]
            S = [i for i in Ls if i not in T]
            n = len(T)
            if n if zero else not (2 <= n <= 5):
                continue
            if {D[i] for i in S} != {1, -1}:
                continue
            if n >= 2 and {D[i] for i in T} != {1, -1}:
                continue
            if n and max(H[i] for i in S) <= min(H[i] for i in T):
                continue                          # a stander must be taller than a turner
            good = True
            break
        if not good:
            continue
        letters = r.sample(AL, nL)
        P = [[" "] * W for _ in range(M)]
        P[M - 1] = ["."] * W
        for j, i in enumerate(Ls):
            t, x0, w = pos[i]
            c = letters[j]
            for u in range(H[i]):
                for v in range(3):
                    P[M - 1 - u][x0 + v] = c
            P[M - 1][x0 + (2 if D[i] > 0 else 0)] = ">" if D[i] > 0 else "<"
        for i in Bs:
            t, x0, w = pos[i]
            for v in range(w):
                P[M - 1 - cl[i]][x0 + v] = "#"
        Q = ["".join(y).rstrip() for y in P]
        while Q and not Q[0]:
            Q.pop(0)                              # no blank rows above the tallest thing
        return "\n".join(Q) + "\n" + "=" * W + "\n" + str(n) + " turn"
    return FB
solve:
def solve(clue):
    P = clue.split("\n")
    T = P.pop()                                   # the "<n> turn" caption, copied through
    B = P.pop()                                   # the tarmac
    W = len(B)
    M = len(P)
    P = [z.ljust(W) for z in P]
    L = P[-1]                                     # the ground row: lorries and open road
    Z = ["".join(z) for z in zip(*P)]             # the picture read column by column
    # clearance of the lowest beam in each column (9 = no beam over this column)
    A = [M - 1 - z.rfind("#") for z in Z]        # M = "no beam here"
    F = list(itertools.accumulate(A, min))                    # lowest beam at or left of j
    G = list(itertools.accumulate(A[::-1], min))[::-1] + [M]  # lowest beam at or right of j
    E = list(L)
    j = 1
    while j < W - 2:
        a = L[j]
        if a == ".":
            j += 1
            continue
        c = L[j + 1]                              # the lorry's letter
        h = M - Z[j + 1].count(" ")               # how tall it is
        # a lorry turns round iff a beam it cannot fit under lies AHEAD of it
        if (G[j + 3] if a != "<" else F[j - 1]) < h:
            E[j:j + 3] = ["<", c, c] if a != "<" else [c, c, ">"]
        j += 3
    return "\n".join(z.rstrip() for z in P[:-1]) + "\n" + "".join(E) + "\n" + B + "\n" + T
